claims.text: A hybrid CE-QHA-ML framework will predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity of HEAs within 5% error.
The hybrid framework will outperform standard CALPHAD extrapolations and pure DFT calculations in both speed and accuracy for multicomponent systems.
Experimental melting data for high-melting, multicomponent HEAs is sparse or unreliable.
An ML correction trained on DFT-QHA residuals can account for anharmonic and magnetic contributions omitted by standard QHA.
Anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions and magnetic disorder become significant near the melting point in multicomponent systems.
Standard CALPHAD models rely on extrapolation from binary and ternary parameters.
Binary and ternary CALPHAD extrapolations often fail to capture nonlinear synergistic effects in HEAs.
Severe lattice distortion and local chemical ordering are examples of nonlinear effects inadequately represented by standard CALPHAD extrapolation.
Pure DFT is too computationally expensive to sample the configurational space needed for melting-point prediction by thermodynamic integration.
Cluster expansion can efficiently map the configurational energy landscape of HEAs.
QHA captures harmonic vibrational free-energy contributions relevant to the proposed calculations.
An ML correction can learn missing anharmonic and magnetic physics from limited high-quality data.
The hybrid model will achieve a melting-temperature MAE below 50 K for novel HEA compositions.
Standard CALPHAD extrapolations will have melting-temperature errors above 150 K.
Pure DFT methods will be computationally infeasible for screening more than 1000 compositions.
Entropy of fusion decreases as atomic-size mismatch increases because of lattice distortion.
The method is valid for substitutional solid-solution HEAs that remain FCC or BCC up to melting.
The method is not applicable when substantial phase separation or intermetallic formation occurs before melting.
ML-correction accuracy depends strongly on training-data diversity and quality, and extrapolation error can increase for remote target compositions.
QHA may fail to capture premelting anharmonic softening in systems with very low Debye temperatures.

contradictions.description: The central prediction requires within 5% error and a melting-temperature MAE below 50 K, but falsification occurs only above 10% or 150 K. Results between these thresholds would violate the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The intervention says the ML correction is intended to account for magnetic contributions, while the boundary excludes cases where magnetic transitions dominate and are not represented in training. This is a limitation on, rather than a complete logical negation of, the claimed magnetic correction capability.
